newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: African oil sector reforms slow - U.N. expert.
newsitem.headline: African oil sector reforms slow - U.N. expert.

text.p: A United Nations consultant said on Tuesday African governments were unwilling to relinquish control of domestic oil pricing due to fears current poor distribution networks would create private monopolies.

"Liberalisation of the oil industry is moving slowly because African governments are afraid private monopolies will replace state monopolies," Claudine Sigam, a consultant with the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development told an oil trade conference in Harare.
Most African governments, including those with oil industries, still determine domestic oil pricing and heavily regulate operations, although a few have started cautious reforms.

Sigam said many governments on the world's poorest continent were afraid liberalising pricing systems to reflect international fluctuations would be unpopular. They were also reluctant to pay subsidies to regions where it would be uneconomic for private companies to operate.
"Consumers here still do not have influence on demand," Sigam said.

Sigam said the challenge for Africa in the long-term was to formulate measures that would tie domestic prices to international price movements, but this was hampered by poor fiscal and monetary policies.
